messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Serving variant freeze request — Vireo-3B-medium compatibility + temporary freeze

Team — quick ask from the ApolloAI POC (external): they want us to serve their Vireo-3B-medium variant for a public demo the first week of May. Sales committed the model variant explicitly and asked us to avoid any automatic rollouts or behind-the-scenes swaps during the demo week.

Concrete ask: can infra/runtime add a temporary route-level freeze (or equivalent pin) on the Vireo-3B-medium variant for the ApolloAI account until 2026-05-11? If a freeze is not feasible, we need a clear compatibility checklist and a plan for a controlled canary + rollback window so the demo isn't interrupted.

Attached: compat_matrix.csv (their initial compatibility notes) — I highlighted the sections about KV cache format and quantization artifacts.

What I need from you by EOD today:
- Dev: feasibility and any infra-side changes required to support a short-term freeze or lock.
- Product (Laura): ops/SLAs we should promise the customer for the demo window and whether we need leadership escalation for any exceptions.
- Monica/Marcus: if this touches routing policies or dedicated pool allocation, ballpark cost and capacity impact.

I'll loop Emma from ApolloAI once we have a proposed approach. Thanks —

Rachel Kim
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Rachel.Kim@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: compat_matrix.csv (CSV summary of ApolloAI artifacts)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Serving variant freeze request — Vireo-3B-medium compatibility + temporary freeze

Rachel / all — thanks for the heads up. Quick technical take:

- Vireo-3B-medium looks broadly compatible with our serving runtime but has two caveats called out in the compat_matrix: (1) the customer supplied a KV cache format that differs in byte-order for the attention cache (we can adapt but need a conversion shim), (2) they provided int4 quant artifacts that assume a specific kernel path that we only use in the quantized runtime.

- Temporary freeze: we can implement a short-lived "variant_lock" flag at the routing layer that prevents automated model promotion or routing to newer weight builds. It's a small change to the routing config + an RBAC check; low-risk. I estimate 2-3 engineer-days to ship and smoke test across staging.

- Alternatives: run a tightly scoped canary (1% traffic -> 5% -> rollback) on a dedicated small pool. That avoids touching the routing code but requires reserve capacity for the canary.

I attached a brief runtime-checklist.md with the conversion/validation steps I want to run against the Apollo artifacts (sample inference runs, KV cache roundtrip tests, kernel fallback checks).

I'll start a staging job to validate the KV conversion if we get their model artifact link.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
dev.patel@redwood.com

Attachments: runtime-checklist.md

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Serving variant freeze request — Vireo-3B-medium compatibility + temporary freeze

Thanks, Rachel and Dev —

From a product/ops standpoint:
- I support a temporary routing-level lock for a customer demo week as long as we: (a) document the window and expiration, (b) limit scope to the specific model_id+variant+account, and (c) add an automated expiration (fail-safe).
- If dev says 2–3 engineer-days, that's acceptable for a short-term exception; we should treat this as an exception path rather than a permanent API change.
- Monica/Marcus: please send cost estimate for a reserved canary pool vs. implementing the routing lock. If cost is negligible, prefer the canary approach for safety.

Next steps:
1) Rachel: get artifact link and demo dates from ApolloAI (Emma).
2) Dev: begin validation run on staging once artifacts are available.
3) Laura: I'll prepare an internal exception doc to cover roll-forward/rollback SLAs and sign-off process; will share to this thread.

If we run into infra constraints that require >3 engineer-days, escalate to Karthik for prioritization.

— Laura

- Laura will own the internal exception doc and sign-off matrix.
- Monica/Marcus: please provide cost + capacity numbers by EOD Apr 23 so we can pick canary vs lock.
